facts.fact: Muse Code offers 4 subscription plans: Everyday Usage, High Usage, Power Usage, and Maximum Usage.
facts.quote: There are 4 subscription plans available for Muse Code:

facts.fact: The Everyday Usage plan lets subscribers send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads.
facts.quote: Send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads

facts.fact: The High Usage plan provides 5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan.
facts.quote: 5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: The Power Usage plan provides 20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan.
facts.quote: 20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: The Maximum Usage plan provides 80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan.
facts.quote: 80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: Muse Code subscribers must be 18 or the age of majority in their country to subscribe.
facts.quote: You must be 18 or the age of majority in your country to subscribe.

facts.fact: Pay-as-you-go billing on Muse Code is charged per token consumed with a Meta Model API key.
facts.quote: billed per token consumed with your Meta Model API key

facts.fact: Any additional API keys a user creates under their Meta Model API account are billed pay-as-you-go rather than under the subscription.
facts.quote: Any additional API keys you create under your Meta Model API account will be billed through pay-as-you-go.

facts.fact: The subscription works only through the Muse Code CLI while signed in with a Meta Model API account.
facts.quote: It works only through the Muse Code CLI while signed in with your Meta Model API account.

facts.fact: Subscription benefits and availability may vary by region.
facts.quote: Subscription benefits and availability may vary by region.

facts.fact: Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode, which gives more plan usage in exchange for letting Meta use the user's content to train future Meta models.
facts.quote: Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode.

facts.fact: Contributor mode can be turned off at any time in Muse Code settings, after which future content is not used to train Meta models.
facts.quote: you can turn it off at any time, at which point your future content is not used to train Meta models

facts.fact: The Power Usage plan includes access to Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant of Muse Wonder.
facts.quote: Access to Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant of Muse Wonder

facts.fact: A headless run on a computer with no settings file has Contributor mode off.
facts.quote: a headless run has Contributor mode off

facts.fact: The MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE environment variable sets Contributor mode for a run, using 1 for on and 0 for off, and a flag given at the same time takes precedence.
facts.quote: You can also set the environment variable `MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE` to `1` (on) or `0` (off) for a run. If you set both, the flag wins.

facts.fact: A subscriber on the Maximum Usage plan who reaches the usage limit must wait for the limit to refresh, because no upgrade is available.
facts.quote: If you are on the Maximum Usage plan, you must wait for your limit to refresh.

facts.fact: Subscribers who reach their plan's usage limit can upgrade to the next plan or wait for the limit to refresh.
facts.quote: If you reach your plan's usage limit, you can upgrade to the next plan, or wait until your limit refreshes.
